questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. You see children playing nearby. What should you do before you start to move your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When you back up, look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially around children. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors for traffic behind you?

options.text: Every 45 seconds
Every 20 seconds
Every 10 seconds
Every 6 to 8 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 6 to 8 seconds
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every 6 to 8 seconds. You need to know if someone is following too close or coming up too fast. You also need to know how much space is behind your car.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights
Other cars on the road
The time of day
The condition of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your ability to stop. Reduce your speed when roads are poor to keep control. Driving too fast on slippery roads and needing to stop is dangerous.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic
On the same side where traffic is moving
On the side facing oncoming traffic
On the side with the heaviest traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic
They follow different traffic laws than larger vehicles
They always have the right-of-way
They don't have rearview mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic
questions.explanation: In many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians, drivers said they were looking but did not see them. These are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lights. Always watch for these smaller, less protected road users.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction
During daylight hours only
At any time
When making turns

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid lines cannot be crossed, except when turning.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in rainy conditions?

options.text: Drive at a speed for ideal weather conditions
Apply brakes as soon as your car skids
Slow down

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: Driving too fast in wet conditions causes your tires to lose contact with the road. Your car rides on water instead of gripping the road. This is called hydroplaning. Slow down in rain to prevent this.

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams comes toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has bright high beams on, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see well enough to stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: You can ignore it in rain, snow, or ice.
It has a triangular shape.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed signs on curves and turns show the recommended speed for that area. You should follow this speed in all weather conditions. In rain, snow, or ice, drive even slower than the posted speed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycles?

options.text: Other drivers can follow a motorcycle closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to show when it slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Your whole vehicle must be in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle on the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be ready to stop. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: You are driving on a road with two solid yellow lines. You may:

options.text: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross them to pass other cars if no traffic is coming.
Never cross them.
Cross them only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed in either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A train station is ahead.
Use your turn signal before going forward.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign warns you about a railroad crossing ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is the safest thing to do when fog is very thick and you cannot see well?

options.text: Drive slowly at under 10 miles per hour.
Use your high beam headlights.
Pull off the road and stop with your emergency flashers on.
Honk your horn every few seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and stop with your emergency flashers on.
questions.explanation: If fog gets so thick you can barely see, pull off the road and turn on your emergency flashers. Stop and wait until visibility gets better. Do not try to drive slowly through the fog.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until you are already in the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is something on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction the arrow points. In this case, it curves left. You may see several of these signs placed throughout the curve.

questions.question: Is it illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles may share a lane, but cars must never share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road as far as safely possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as far as safely possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is using lights and/or sirens, move to the right side of the road as close as you can safely get and stop. Do not stop inside an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop Sign Ahead
Side Road
Railroad Warning

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should look for a gap of ____ seconds.

options.text: One to two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Look for a four-second gap in traffic before changing lanes. This gives you and the car behind you a safe two-second following distance when you merge.

questions.question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road
Near the centerline
On the left of the centerline

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline
questions.explanation: Position your car in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn as your front reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: When is it acceptable to park in an access aisle next to a handicap parking spot?

options.text: Never
When you have a disability plate or parking placard
When all other parking spaces are full
When you are only parking for a couple minutes

questions.correctAnswerText: Never
questions.explanation: Never park in an access aisle. This is against the law and can result in a fine of at least $200.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road
On paved highways
When driving at night
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on surfaces with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when driving behind a large vehicle:

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing them
Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers may not see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your distance to see around the sides and view the road ahead.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic
When turning left into a driveway
When the car in front of you is disabled
When passing to the right on a one-way street

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: You are making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street. When you have completed the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the right lane of the street
In the center of the street
In the left lane of the street
In the lane with the least traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane of the street
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection and no markings appear to indicate a stop line or crosswalk, a driver:

options.text: Is not required to stop
Is required to slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear
Should stop only at a place where they can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if they have to enter the intersecting roadway
Should stop where they have a clear view of approaching traffic before they enter the intersecting roadway

questions.correctAnswerText: Should stop where they have a clear view of approaching traffic before they enter the intersecting roadway
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point nearest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp where there is no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match the flow of traffic
Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic
Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you find a gap in traffic. You should wait and be stopped while looking for a safe gap to appear.
